domain_label: Study System — Engagement, Gamification & Progress Visuals (engage): mechanics and their hazards
purpose: A method for choosing which engagement and progress-visual mechanics to build into a single-user study app — the owner's calendar day-box with a green download-bar fill, a completion tick and 5%-increment percentages, plus streaks/freezes, habit-loop cueing, confidence-rated mastery and a course-level view — and, equally, for deciding what NOT to copy, so each mechanic is grounded in the cited literature (goal-gradient, habit formation) or vendor precedent (Duolingo, GitHub, Anki), the anti-patterns (overjustification, streak anxiety, gamification-over-learning) are built in as guardrails rather than discovered in production, and every claim is tagged FACT / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN exactly as the grounding research file did, inventing no engagement statistic the file did not verify.
assumptions: the single learner is the only user and there is no leaderboard, social comparison or tangible-reward economy in scope; every mechanic is judged as informational feedback to one person, not as a competitive or points-for-prizes system

the owner's day-box calendar brief (white empty box, green download-bar fill, tick at 100%, percentage in 5% increments, day/task/course visuals) is a binding verbatim requirement to render faithfully, not a design to re-open

psychology effect sizes are taken from the cited primary papers (Kivetz 2006 goal-gradient, Lally 2010 habit formation, Lepper 1973 and Deci/Koestner/Ryan 1999 overjustification) as reported, and applied as design priors, never as guarantees for this specific app's behavior
vendor engagement numbers (e.g. Duolingo's 7-day-streak 2.4x-more-likely figure) are the vendor's own claims via search snippets, not independent findings, and are used for direction only

the specific confidence-rating scale and several owner-open points (5%-step rounding direction, whether past-incomplete days freeze or gray out) are build-time decisions the research file did not fix and are carried as ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN, never invented
exclusions: the multimodal spoken-answer capture and queue architecture (record -> batch transcribe -> LLM-grade -> write back), the STT engine choice (whisper.cpp / faster-whisper / cloud), language coverage counts and voice-privacy/GDPR posture belong to the multimodal-capture specialist and are not modelled here except where a grade feeds the mastery state the course-view consumes

the spaced-repetition scheduling algorithm itself (interval math, backlog ordering) belongs to the scheduler/SRS specialist; this KB only constrains that engagement mechanics must never degrade its output (the non-punitive-backlog rule)
the flashcard-quality and book-decomposition rules that populate the learner model belong to their own specialist and are referenced only as the upstream source of the mastery denominator
front-end implementation detail (exact CSS, animation framing, component library) beyond the state model and rendering policy the owner's spec fixes
inventing an engagement lift, retention rate, streak-length distribution, pass rate or effect size the research file did not verify, or presenting a vendor claim as an independent finding

competency_questions.question: What exactly did the owner specify for the day-box calendar, and which of those elements are binding versus open?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OWNER_SPEC_FIDELITY states the white-empty / green-download-bar-fill / tick-at-100% / 5%-increment-percentage / day-task-course visuals as the binding verbatim brief (FACT), and names the open points (rounding direction, past-incomplete-day behaviour) as ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN to resolve at build time, not to redesign

competency_questions.question: What is the per-day-box data model and how many fill states does the 5%-increment rule produce?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DAY_BOX_DATA_MODEL gives {date, tasks_total, tasks_done, pct=floor((done/total)*20)*5, state: empty|partial|complete}, derives the 21 states (0,5,...,95,tick), tags floor rounding as an ESTIMATE and unweighted count as the literal reading, and PARTIAL_DAY_STATE_POLICY carries the frozen-vs-gray-out UNKNOWN

competency_questions.question: Why must the day-view (effort) metric and the course-view (mastery) metric be kept separate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EFFORT_VS_MASTERY_SEPARATION states day-box % is completion effort against that day's task denominator while course % is mastery from the learner model, that they are DIFFERENT metrics that must not be conflated, and COURSE_LEVEL_VISUAL derives the course % from the KB coverage/mastery model reusing the 5%-step display

competency_questions.question: Why should a visible partial fill and a 5%-step numeral increase effort, and what is the evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOAL_GRADIENT_LEVER cites Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006 (JMR) that effort accelerates the closer one is to a reward as a FACT, ties the partial green fill to that pull, and PROGRESS_FILL_VISUAL renders it as informational progress feedback per the owner's spec

competency_questions.question: How should the streak and streak-freeze work, and what does the Duolingo precedent actually claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STREAK_MECHANIC defines the consecutive-day streak, cites Duolingo's loss-aversion framing and the 7-day-streak-2.4x figure as a vendor claim (not independent), and STREAK_FREEZE_REPAIR requires a freeze equipped in advance / consumed per miss rather than a retroactive or hard reset

competency_questions.question: How does the cue-routine-reward habit loop map onto the app, and how long before the habit is self-sustaining?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HABIT_LOOP_MAPPING maps push-notification/app-open = cue, the day's task queue = routine, the advancing green fill + tick = reward (tagging the Duhigg attribution ESTIMATE), and SAME_CONTEXT_REPETITION cites Lally 2010's 66-day median (range 18-254) and the consistent-daily-slot consequence

competency_questions.question: What is the overjustification hazard and which guardrail keeps the visuals from undermining intrinsic motivation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OVERJUSTIFICATION_HAZARD cites Lepper 1973 and the Deci/Koestner/Ryan 1999 meta-analysis (128 experiments; expected tangible rewards undermine free-choice intrinsic motivation) as FACT and prescribes keeping the visuals as informational progress feedback rather than adding points/prizes for studying

competency_questions.question: What is streak anxiety, and how is a broken streak prevented from becoming a demotivator?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STREAK_ANXIETY_HAZARD states that a broken streak can flip the feature into a demotivator (Oulu thesis; quitting accounts) and SECONDARY_HORIZON_METRIC prescribes a long-horizon metric (e.g. days-active-in-last-30) that a single miss cannot zero

competency_questions.question: What is the gamification-over-learning hazard and how is scheduling protected from it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GAMIFICATION_OVER_LEARNING states that engagement mechanics must never degrade real learning or scheduling quality, and NON_PUNITIVE_SCHEDULER_CONTRACT mandates that a broken streak never reduces SRS backlog quality and the backlog view stays non-punitive

competency_questions.question: Which prior-art patterns does the owner's spec rhyme with, and where does it deliberately differ?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRIBUTION_GRAPH_PRECEDENT states GitHub encodes relative volume by quartile-recalibrated colour while the owner wants absolute per-day completion, and ANKI_HEATMAP_PRECEDENT confirms the calendar pattern works in spaced-repetition study and plots future scheduled load, not just past

competency_questions.question: Is illusionary progress usable, and where is the ethical line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ILLUSIONARY_PROGRESS_ETHICS notes Kivetz 2006 showed illusionary progress (a 12-stamp card with 2 pre-stamped) accelerates behaviour, but rules that fabricating fake progress on a self-study tool is a manipulation risk and progress must map to real task denominators

competency_questions.question: How is mastery (as opposed to effort) rated, and what part of the rating scale is not fixed by the research?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_RATED_MASTERY explains that course-view mastery comes from the learner model fed by self-rated confidence and/or LLM grading, and flags that the specific confidence-rating scale is a build-time decision the research file did not fix (UNKNOWN)

competency_questions.question: When is an engagement feature a go, and what makes it a no-go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENGAGEMENT_GO_NOGO composes the verdict: a mechanic ships only when it renders the owner spec faithfully, is informational not tangible-reward, carries a freeze/repair plus secondary-metric guardrail, and never degrades scheduling; a mechanic that fails any gate is a no-go until fixed

glossary.definition: One box per day in a calendar (month or week) view: white when empty (with the day number in it), filling like a green downloading bar as the day's tasks complete, showing the percentage in 5% increments while partial, and replaced/overlaid by a tick at 100%. The owner's binding verbatim brief [FACT — owner brief], rendered faithfully, not redesigned.

The derived render state of a day-box from pct = floor((done/total)*20)*5: the 20 partial numerals 0,5,10,...,95 plus the distinguished terminal tick = 21 states. Floor rounding (67% -> 65) is an ESTIMATE recommended so the tick and '100' appear only at true completion; unweighted task count is the literal reading of the spec.

Two distinct metrics that must not be conflated: day-view effort = completion % against that day's assigned task denominator; course-view mastery = units mastered / total from the learner model. A perfect day-box streak does not imply course mastery [ESTIMATE — design, high confidence per research file].

Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (2006), Journal of Marketing Research 43(1):39-58: real-world effort accelerates the closer a person is to a reward, and illusionary progress (pre-stamped card) also accelerates it [FACT]. Design use: a visible partial fill pulls the learner to finish today's tasks.

The three-part frame popularised by Duhigg's The Power of Habit (2012) [ESTIMATE — attribution, high confidence]: mapped here as push-notification/app-open = cue, the day's task queue = routine, advancing green fill + tick = reward. Same-context repetition is what Lally 2010 actually measured.

A streak = consecutive days with at least one completed session; it resets to zero on a missed day unless a freeze is equipped in advance and consumed one-per-miss (Duolingo model; freezes cannot be applied retroactively) [FACT — via search snippet, blog.duolingo.com 403]. Duolingo claims a 7-day streak makes a learner 2.4x more likely to continue (vendor claim, not independent).

Lepper, Greene & Nisbett (1973) and the Deci, Koestner & Ryan (1999) meta-analysis of 128 experiments: expected tangible rewards significantly undermine free-choice intrinsic motivation (engagement-contingent d=-0.40, completion-contingent d=-0.36, performance-contingent d=-0.28) [FACT]. Guardrail: keep visuals informational, not points/prizes for studying.

The failure mode where a broken streak flips a motivational feature into a demotivator (University of Oulu thesis on Duolingo streak motivation; abundant first-person quit-after-a-long-streak accounts) [FACT — via search snippets]. Mitigated by freeze/repair, a secondary long-horizon metric, and a non-punitive backlog.

A long-window engagement number (e.g. days active in the last 30) shown alongside the streak so a single miss cannot zero the learner's sense of progress [ESTIMATE — design guardrail from the research file].

The binding rule that no engagement mechanic may reduce actual scheduling quality: a broken streak must not change what the SRS surfaces next, and the backlog/review view stays non-punitive [ESTIMATE — design; grounds the gamification-over-learning guardrail].

nodes.definition: Anchor the whole engagement design to the owner's unusually concrete verbatim brief and render it faithfully rather than redesigning it [FACT — owner brief]. Binding elements: a calendar view (one month OR one week) with one box per day; an empty box is white (with, most naturally, the day number in it); as the day's tasks/revision complete the box fills like a downloading bar, green; at 100% a tick (checkmark) replaces/overlays the fill; while partial, show the percentage in 5% increments; the visuals span the course, the days, tasks completed and the percentage. Open points the owner did NOT specify are held, not invented: the 5%-step rounding direction (recommend floor, 67->65, so the tick/'100' mark only true completion — ESTIMATE, medium-high confidence), whether 'one in it' means a day-number label (ESTIMATE, high confidence), and whether past incomplete days freeze at their percentage or gray out (UNKNOWN). This node fixes what is contract versus what is a build-time call.

included: the binding white/green-fill/tick/5%-increment/day-task-course elements as verbatim brief
the separation of binding elements from owner-open points
the ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags on the open points
excluded: the exact data model fields (its own node)
the psychology of why the design works

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an owner clarification or a build decision changes what is binding versus open

pros.claim: Treating the concrete brief as contract prevents an engineer redesigning a feature the owner already specified precisely
pros.example: building the green download-bar fill exactly, rather than substituting a ring or a star the owner did not ask for

cons.claim: A verbatim brief still leaves genuine gaps that must be resolved without inventing owner intent
cons.example: guessing that past incomplete days gray out when the owner never said so and a frozen-percentage reading is equally valid

failure_modes: redesigning a specified element (colour, fill metaphor, tick) the owner fixed
inventing an answer to an owner-open point instead of flagging it for build-time resolution
acceptance_tests: the analysis lists the binding white/green-fill/tick/5%-increment/day-task-course elements as FACT and separates them from the rounding-direction and past-day open points tagged ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: the owner clarifies a previously open point
a build-time decision needs the brief re-read

nodes.definition: Define the per-day-box data model that turns the brief into a renderable state [ESTIMATE — design derived from the FACT brief]: {date, tasks_total, tasks_done, weight_done?, pct = floor((done/total)*20)*5, state: empty | partial(pct) | complete}. The 5%-increment rule with floor rounding yields exactly 21 fill states — the twenty partial numerals 0,5,10,...,95 plus the distinguished terminal tick. Unweighted task count is the literal reading of the spec; task weighting (a 40-minute revision versus a 2-minute check-in) is a build-time decision left optional (weight_done?). The model is the single source the fill height, the numeral and the tick all read from, so day, task and percentage visuals never diverge.

included: the {date, tasks_total, tasks_done, weight_done?, pct, state} fields
the 21-fill-state derivation and floor-rounding basis
the unweighted-count literal reading and optional task weighting
excluded: the partial/past-day rendering policy (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a weighting decision or a new per-day visual changes the model

pros.claim: One state model feeding fill, numeral and tick keeps the three day-box visuals consistent by construction
pros.example: the numeral '65' and a 65%-height green fill both reading the same pct field so they cannot disagree

cons.claim: Choosing unweighted count for simplicity can misrepresent a day where one long task dominates the real effort
cons.example: a day-box showing 50% because 1 of 2 tasks is done when the undone task is a 3-hour revision

failure_modes: letting fill height and numeral compute from different sources and drift apart
hard-coding unweighted count when the course needs weighted effort and vice versa
acceptance_tests: the model states the field set, derives the 21 states from floor((done/total)*20)*5, and marks unweighted count the literal reading with task weighting an optional build-time field
revisit_triggers: a task-weighting decision is made at build time

nodes.definition: Resolve the rendering policy for partial and past-incomplete days, keeping the genuine unknowns visible [floor rounding ESTIMATE; past-day behaviour UNKNOWN]. Rounding direction: recommend floor (67% -> 65) so the tick and a full bar signify only true 100% completion, matching the owner's distinguished terminal tick; this is an ESTIMATE (medium-high confidence), not an owner statement. Past incomplete days: the owner did not specify whether they stay frozen at their last percentage or gray out — hold as UNKNOWN and design the model so either can be switched on without a rewrite (store the frozen pct regardless of the visual treatment). The 5%-increment display is the granularity the owner fixed and must not be made finer or coarser.

the frozen-vs-gray-out past-day UNKNOWN and the switch-either-way design
the fixed 5%-increment granularity
excluded: the underlying state fields (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an owner decision or a user-testing signal resolves a held-open point

pros.claim: Storing the frozen percentage regardless of visual treatment lets the frozen-vs-gray-out choice be a config flag, not a rewrite
pros.example: keeping pct on a past day so switching from gray-out to frozen-display later needs no data migration

cons.claim: Floor rounding is a recommendation, not an owner instruction, so a ceiling or nearest preference could overturn it
cons.example: the owner later preferring 67 -> 70 so partial days feel more generous, reversing the floor default

failure_modes: hard-coding a past-day visual treatment before the owner decides

nodes.definition: Read the GitHub contribution graph as the canonical calendar-of-coloured-day-boxes the owner's spec rhymes with, and mark where it deliberately differs [FACT — via search snippet; official docs page 403]. GitHub colours each day-square by contribution count on a scale RELATIVE to the user's own activity: after excluding zero days, counts are split into 4 quartiles giving 4 green-intensity levels, and the scale RECALIBRATES as the rolling window moves. The owner's day-box instead encodes ABSOLUTE completion — the percentage of that day's assigned tasks — by fill height plus a numeral. The owner's version is the better fit for a task system because each day has a defined denominator, whereas GitHub's relative colour has none [ESTIMATE — analysis, high confidence]. Copy the calendar-of-boxes layout; do NOT copy the relative-quartile colour semantics.

the contrast with the owner's absolute per-day completion
the copy-layout / do-not-copy-colour-semantics conclusion
excluded: the Anki heatmap precedent (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the official doc is fetched or a relative-vs-absolute review changes the borrow

pros.example: keeping the year-of-boxes grid but replacing relative quartile colour with an absolute per-day fill and numeral

cons.claim: The relative-recalibration detail is grounded in community discussions with the official doc page 403, so the exact quartile mechanic is snippet-grade not directly fetched

nodes.definition: Use the Anki Review Heatmap add-on as proof the calendar-of-day-boxes pattern already works in spaced-repetition study, and mirror its most useful feature [FACT — fetched github.com/glutanimate/review-heatmap]. The add-on (Glutanimate, AGPLv3) adds a GitHub-contribution-style heatmap to Anki's main window that visualises past AND FUTURE card-review activity, shows streak data, and lets a click on a day reveal that day's cards; it is built on d3.js + cal-heatmap. The notable feature to copy is that it plots FUTURE scheduled load, not only past completion — useful for the owner's scheduling system to show tomorrow's forecast burden [ESTIMATE — design]. So the day-box view should be able to show upcoming scheduled workload, not just a backward record of completion.

nodes.definition: Establish the foundational distinction the whole visual system must respect: the day-view is an EFFORT/completion metric and the course-view is a MASTERY metric, and they must not be conflated [ESTIMATE — design, high confidence per research file]. The day-box percentage measures completion against that day's assigned task denominator — it says the learner did the work scheduled for today. Course-level percentage measures mastery — units mastered over total units — derived from the learner model, not from how many boxes are green. A learner can run a perfect green streak of effort while course mastery lags (cramming, forgetting, shallow completion). Because they answer different questions, they need different denominators and must be shown as distinct figures, never merged into one 'progress' number.

included: the effort-vs-mastery definition and their separate denominators
the perfect-effort-but-lagging-mastery case
the never-merge-into-one-number rule
excluded: how the course-level view is rendered (its own node)
how mastery is rated (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a unify-the-metrics push or a mastery-computation change tests the separation

pros.claim: Keeping effort and mastery separate stops a green day-box streak from being misread as course competence
pros.example: showing '90% of this week's tasks done' and 'unit mastery 40%' as two figures so effort does not masquerade as mastery

cons.claim: Two progress numbers are more cognitively demanding than one and can confuse a learner who wants a single sense of progress
cons.example: a learner unsure which of the effort and mastery figures 'really' measures their progress

failure_modes: merging effort and mastery into one progress bar that flatters completion

acceptance_tests: the node defines day-view effort against a task denominator and course-view mastery from the learner model, gives the perfect-effort-lagging-mastery case, and forbids merging them into one number
revisit_triggers: a design push to show a single unified progress number

nodes.definition: Render the owner's green download-bar fill, 5%-increment numeral and completion tick as INFORMATIONAL progress feedback — the mechanic the psychology literature treats favourably [FACT — owner brief for the visual; ESTIMATE — informational-framing per Deci/Ryan literature]. The box fills bottom-up in green as the day's tasks complete, the numeral steps in 5% increments while partial, and the tick replaces/overlays the fill at 100%. Crucially, the fill communicates progress information; it is not a points-or-prizes reward, which keeps it on the favourable side of the overjustification literature. This node is where the brief becomes a concrete visual and is the surface every psychology lever (goal-gradient, habit-loop reward) and every hazard (overjustification) attaches to.

included: the green fill / 5%-numeral / tick as the rendered informational-feedback visual
the not-a-tangible-reward framing
its role as the attachment surface for levers and hazards

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reward-ification proposal or a chase-the-bar signal tests the framing

pros.example: the advancing bar telling the learner how far they are, not paying them points for finishing

nodes.definition: Ground the partial fill in the goal-gradient effect: effort accelerates the closer a person is to a reward [FACT — Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006, Journal of Marketing Research 43(1):39-58]. In their real cafe reward program customers purchased more frequently the closer they were to the free coffee, and rated more, visited more often and persisted longer as they approached a reward; the title's 'resurrected' revives Hull's 1930s animal goal-gradient work for humans. Implication for the day-box: a visible partial fill (35%... 60%...) exploits goal-gradient — the nearer the bar is to full, the stronger the pull to finish today's tasks — and the 5%-step numeral makes progress feel granular and always-moving [ESTIMATE — direct application, high confidence]. This is the primary evidence-backed reason the owner's design should work.

included: the Kivetz 2006 goal-gradient finding as FACT
the partial-fill-and-5%-numeral application to the day-box
its status as the primary evidence for the design

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an in-app behaviour measurement or a redesign of the partial fill changes the lever

cons.claim: The evidence is from consumer reward programs, not self-directed study, so the transfer is a reasoned application not a measured result for this app
cons.example: assuming a study learner responds to a task-completion bar exactly as café customers did to a coffee card

failure_modes: overstating the café-program effect as a guaranteed study-behaviour result
hiding partial progress so the goal-gradient pull is never triggered
acceptance_tests: the node cites Kivetz 2006's acceleration-near-reward finding as FACT and applies it to the visible partial fill and 5%-step numeral, tagging the study-transfer as a reasoned application
revisit_triggers: an in-app measurement of completion-near-full behaviour lands

nodes.definition: Define the streak: a count of consecutive days with at least one completed session, modelled on Duolingo [FACT — via search snippet, blog.duolingo.com 403]. The streak resets to zero on a missed day (unless protected — see the freeze node). Duolingo explicitly frames the mechanic as tapping LOSS AVERSION and claims learners who reach a 7-day streak are 2.4x more likely to continue the next day than learners without a streak — a VENDOR claim via search snippet, to be used for direction only, not as an independent finding. The streak reinforces the habit loop by giving the daily routine a running score the learner does not want to lose. Because the same loss-aversion force is exactly what turns toxic when the streak breaks, this node is deliberately paired with the freeze/repair and streak-anxiety guardrails.

included: the consecutive-day definition and reset-on-miss rule
the Duolingo loss-aversion framing and the 2.4x vendor claim (direction only)
the pairing with freeze/repair and anxiety guardrails

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an independent streak figure or an in-app break signal changes the mechanic

pros.claim: A running streak gives the daily routine a concrete, loss-averse stake that a precedent brand found to correlate with continuation
pros.example: a 7-day counter the learner protects by studying today rather than losing the run

cons.claim: The same loss-aversion stake becomes a liability when the streak breaks, so the mechanic cannot ship without its guardrails
cons.example: a learner who quits entirely after a long streak resets to zero

failure_modes: shipping the streak without the freeze/repair and secondary-metric guardrails
citing the vendor 2.4x figure as an independent, generalisable result
acceptance_tests: the node defines the consecutive-day streak and reset-on-miss, cites the Duolingo loss-aversion framing and the 2.4x figure as a vendor claim for direction only, and pairs the mechanic with its guardrails
revisit_triggers: an independent (non-vendor) streak-retention figure becomes available
an in-app streak-break behaviour signal appears

nodes.definition: Specify the freeze/repair guardrail that keeps the streak from becoming a hard-reset trap [FACT — Duolingo freeze mechanic via search snippet; ESTIMATE — the offer-it-here design]. On the Duolingo model a streak freeze must be equipped in ADVANCE (acquired from the shop before a miss, not retroactively) and is consumed one per missed day, protecting the streak from a single lapse. For this single-user study app the design consequence [ESTIMATE — design, from the research file's guardrail list] is to offer freeze/repair mechanics rather than hard resets, so an unavoidable missed day does not zero a long run. Because early habit formation is fragile (see the same-context/66-day node), streak protection matters most in the first ~2 months. Freeze/repair is the direct antidote to streak anxiety and is a required companion to the streak mechanic.

included: the equip-in-advance / consumed-per-miss freeze rule (FACT via snippet)
the offer-freeze/repair-not-hard-reset design consequence

nodes.definition: Set the same-context repetition default from the habit-formation evidence [FACT — Lally, van Jaarsveld, Potts & Wardle (2010), European Journal of Social Psychology]. nodes.definition: Build in the overjustification guardrail: do NOT bolt tangible rewards onto an activity the learner may already find intrinsically interesting [FACT]. Lepper, Greene & Nisbett (1973), JPSP 28(1):129-137, found children promised an extrinsic reward for an activity they already enjoyed showed reduced subsequent intrinsic interest, while unexpected rewards did not cause the drop. Deci, Koestner & Ryan (1999), a meta-analysis of 128 experiments in Psychological Bulletin 125(6):627-668, found expected tangible rewards significantly undermined free-choice intrinsic motivation (engagement-contingent d=-0.40, completion-contingent d=-0.36, performance-contingent d=-0.28). The guardrail [ESTIMATE — application, high confidence]: keep the day-box, streak and course visuals as INFORMATIONAL feedback on progress — which the same literature treats far more favourably — rather than adding points, coins or prizes for studying. This is the hazard the progress-fill and streak mechanics are deliberately kept clear of.

nodes.definition: Name the streak-anxiety hazard so the streak's guardrails are non-optional [FACT — via search snippets]. Duolingo itself frames streaks via loss aversion; a University of Oulu thesis on Duolingo streak motivation found that broken streaks can flip the feature into a demotivator ('having your motivational feature be the reason a learner is completely demotivated should raise concerns'), and there are abundant first-person accounts of quitting entirely after a long streak breaks. The failure is that the very loss-aversion force that drives daily return turns punitive at the break point. Guardrails required [ESTIMATE — design, from the research file]: offer freeze/repair rather than hard resets, show a secondary long-horizon metric a single miss cannot zero, and never let a broken streak reduce actual scheduling quality. This hazard is why the streak mechanic ships only with its companions.

nodes.definition: Draw the ethical line around illusionary progress [FACT — Kivetz 2006 finding; ESTIMATE — the ethics boundary]. Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (2006) showed illusionary progress works: a 12-stamp card with 2 stamps pre-given accelerated behaviour more than an equivalent 10-stamp card — endowed head-start progress pulls harder. The temptation is to fabricate head-start or inflated progress in the day-box to exploit the same pull. The ruling for a single-user self-study tool [ESTIMATE — design]: fabricating fake progress is a manipulation of the learner by their own tool and corrodes the effort-vs-mastery honesty the system depends on, so progress must map to REAL task denominators — the fill shows genuinely completed work, not a manufactured head start. Honest goal-gradient (a truthful partial fill) is encouraged; illusionary goal-gradient (invented progress) is out of scope.

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go the whole KB builds toward: an engagement or progress-visual mechanic is a GO only when it clears four gates at once [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. (1) Fidelity: it renders the owner's binding brief faithfully (white empty box, green download-bar fill, tick at 100%, 5%-increment percentage, day/task/course visuals) and does not redesign a fixed element. (2) Motivation safety: it is informational progress feedback, not a tangible points/prizes reward (overjustification gate). (3) Guardrails: any streak-like mechanic carries freeze/repair plus a secondary long-horizon metric, and progress maps to real denominators (streak-anxiety and illusionary-progress gates). (4) Learning primacy: it never degrades scheduling — a broken streak or low day never changes the SRS backlog, which stays non-punitive, and effort visuals never masquerade as mastery. A mechanic that is engaging but fails any gate is a NO-GO until fixed. Vendor engagement numbers (e.g. Duolingo's 2.4x) inform direction only and never substitute for clearing the gates.

edge_cases.trigger: a hard reset with no freeze/repair fires on a single miss
edge_cases.mitigation: offer freeze/repair equipped in advance and show a secondary long-horizon metric a single miss cannot zero

edge_cases.description: A points/coins economy is added on top of task completion to boost engagement
edge_cases.trigger: a tangible-reward feature is proposed for studying an already-interesting activity
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the visuals informational progress feedback and reject a points/prizes economy per the overjustification meta-analysis

edge_cases.description: A broken streak or low-completion day silently reduces or reorders the SRS backlog
edge_cases.trigger: an engagement state is allowed to influence what the scheduler surfaces
edge_cases.mitigation: guarantee engagement state never changes the backlog, which stays ordered by learning need and non-punitive

edge_cases.description: The day-box seeds a fabricated head-start fill to exploit illusionary progress
edge_cases.trigger: a designer adds pre-filled progress not backed by completed work
edge_cases.mitigation: map every fill segment to real completed tasks and treat fabricated head-start progress as out of scope

edge_cases.description: Course mastery is computed from green-box effort count rather than the learner model
edge_cases.trigger: the course % is wired to completion instead of mastery ratings/grades
edge_cases.mitigation: derive the course % from units-times-mastery-state in the learner model, keeping it independent of box count

edge_cases.description: The 5%-increment rounding direction is left undefined and the tick appears before true 100%
edge_cases.trigger: a ceiling or nearest rounding lets 97% render as 100 and show the tick early
edge_cases.mitigation: use floor rounding so the tick and a full bar signify only genuine 100% completion

edge_cases.description: Past incomplete days are hard-coded to gray out before the owner has decided their behaviour
edge_cases.trigger: a past-day visual is committed while the owner-open point is still UNKNOWN
edge_cases.mitigation: store the frozen percentage regardless of treatment so frozen-display vs gray-out remains a config flag, not a rewrite

edge_cases.description: A vendor engagement number (Duolingo's 2.4x) is quoted as an independent, generalisable result
edge_cases.trigger: a vendor claim via search snippet is presented as verified evidence
edge_cases.mitigation: label the figure a vendor claim for direction only and never let it substitute for clearing a go/no-go gate

edge_cases.description: A future-scheduled-load forecast is stacked onto the completion box and makes it unreadable
edge_cases.trigger: the Anki-style forecast layer is merged into the primary completion fill
edge_cases.mitigation: show forecast load as a distinct secondary indicator so the primary fill stays a clear truthful completion signal

edge_cases.description: The habit is assumed to form in a week and early streak protection is dropped too soon
edge_cases.trigger: the ~66-day habit timeline is ignored in favour of a fast-forming assumption
edge_cases.mitigation: front-load freeze/repair and the guardrails through the fragile ~2-month window per the Lally 2010 66-day median and wide range

workflow.action: Fix the binding owner brief and separate it from open points
workflow.description: List the white/green-fill/tick/5%-increment/day-task-course elements as contract and the rounding and past-day questions as ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the binding elements are stated as FACT and the open points are flagged, none invented

workflow.action: Define the per-day-box state model and rendering policy
workflow.description: Specify {date, tasks_total, tasks_done, weight_done?, pct, state}, derive the 21 fill states, and set floor rounding and the frozen-vs-gray-out UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the fields, 21 states, floor-rounding ESTIMATE and past-day UNKNOWN are stated and fill/numeral read one source

workflow.action: Read the GitHub and Anki precedents
workflow.description: Contrast GitHub's relative quartile colour with absolute completion and confirm the Anki SRS heatmap and its future-load feature
workflow.gate: the borrow-layout / reject-relative-colour call and the future-load feature are stated with FACT/ESTIMATE tags

workflow.action: Separate the effort and mastery metrics
workflow.description: Define day-view effort vs course-view mastery, their separate denominators, and the never-merge rule
workflow.gate: the two metrics, their denominators and the never-conflate rule are stated

workflow.action: Render the progress fill and course view
workflow.description: Render the green fill/numeral/tick as informational feedback and derive the course % from the mastery state
workflow.gate: the fill is framed informational-not-tangible and the course % derives from mastery not box count

workflow.action: Ground the goal-gradient lever and the illusionary-progress line
workflow.description: Cite Kivetz 2006 for the partial-fill pull and rule fabricated progress out of scope
workflow.gate: the goal-gradient FACT is cited and progress is required to map to real denominators

workflow.action: Map the habit loop and set the same-context default
workflow.description: Map cue/routine/reward, tag the Duhigg attribution, and set the consistent daily slot per Lally 2010
workflow.gate: the loop mapping, the ESTIMATE attribution, and the 66-day / consistent-slot default are stated

workflow.action: Define the streak with freeze/repair and a secondary metric
workflow.description: Define the consecutive-day streak, cite the vendor figure for direction only, and attach freeze/repair and the long-horizon metric
workflow.gate: the streak, the vendor-claim caveat, and the freeze/repair plus secondary-metric guardrails are all present

workflow.action: Rate mastery and specify the confidence-rating input
workflow.description: Feed mastery from self-confidence rating and/or LLM grading and flag the rating scale UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: mastery is derived from ratings/grades and the specific scale is flagged an UNKNOWN build-time decision

workflow.action: Build the hazard guardrails into a contract
workflow.description: State the overjustification, streak-anxiety and gamification-over-learning hazards and merge their guardrails
workflow.gate: each hazard is cited with its FACT/ESTIMATE grade and its guardrail specified

workflow.action: Compose the non-punitive contract and the go/no-go
workflow.description: Merge the guardrails into the non-punitive scheduler contract and the four-gate verdict
workflow.gate: the verdict intersects fidelity, motivation-safety, guardrail and learning-primacy gates and rules a fail on any a no-go

priority_rationale: The owner-spec fidelity, the day-box data model and its rendering policy come first because every visual and mechanic must faithfully encode the binding brief before anything is built on it; the prior-art precedents and the effort-vs-mastery separation next, because they decide what to borrow and fix the core metric distinction the whole system rests on; the progress-fill visual, goal-gradient lever, habit-loop mapping and same-context default then turn the brief into evidence-grounded mechanics; the streak, freeze/repair, secondary metric, confidence-rated mastery and course view apply those mechanics; the overjustification, streak-anxiety, illusionary-progress and gamification-over-learning hazards then install the guardrails; and the non-punitive scheduler contract and the four-gate go/no-go come last because they compose every mechanic and guardrail into one testable contract and a defensible ship/no-ship verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: The binding owner brief dominates any designer improvement of a specified element
dominance_rules.rationale: the owner specified the visual concretely, so a fixed element is contract not a suggestion
dominance_rules.trigger: an engineer proposes changing a specified colour, fill metaphor or the tick
dominance_rules.action: render the specified element faithfully and confine design freedom to the owner-open points

dominance_rules.rationale: the system exists to teach, so no mechanic may degrade real learning or scheduling
dominance_rules.trigger: a mechanic would improve an engagement metric at the cost of the SRS backlog or mastery
dominance_rules.action: reject or rework the mechanic so engagement state never changes what the scheduler surfaces

dominance_rules.rationale: the overjustification meta-analysis shows expected tangible rewards undermine intrinsic motivation while informational feedback is treated favourably
dominance_rules.trigger: a points/coins/prizes economy is proposed for studying
dominance_rules.action: keep the visuals informational and refuse the tangible-reward economy

dominance_rules.rule: The mastery metric dominates the effort metric for course progress
dominance_rules.rationale: effort completion and mastery are different questions with different denominators
dominance_rules.trigger: course progress is about to be computed from green-box effort count
dominance_rules.action: derive course progress from the learner model's mastery state, not from box count

dominance_rules.rule: Streak guardrails dominate the bare streak
dominance_rules.rationale: the same loss-aversion stake that drives return demotivates at the break
dominance_rules.trigger: a streak is proposed without freeze/repair and a secondary metric
dominance_rules.action: require freeze/repair and a secondary long-horizon metric before the streak ships

dominance_rules.rationale: fabricated head-start progress manipulates the learner via their own tool and corrodes effort-vs-mastery honesty
dominance_rules.trigger: pre-filled or fabricated progress is proposed to boost the goal-gradient pull
dominance_rules.action: map every fill segment to real completed work and treat fabricated progress as out of scope

dominance_rules.rule: Independent evidence dominates a vendor claim
dominance_rules.rationale: vendor engagement numbers are the vendor's own claims via search snippets, not independent findings
dominance_rules.trigger: a vendor figure is cited as verified evidence for a decision
dominance_rules.action: use the vendor number for direction only, keep its grade explicit, and never let it clear a go/no-go gate

dominance_rules.rule: Floor rounding dominates for the completion-tick threshold
dominance_rules.rationale: the tick is the owner's distinguished terminal state and must mark only true 100%
dominance_rules.trigger: a rounding direction is being chosen for the 5% steps
dominance_rules.action: use floor rounding so the tick and a full bar appear only at genuine completion

dominance_rules.rule: The non-punitive backlog dominates any streak or engagement state
dominance_rules.rationale: scheduling quality must never depend on whether a streak survived
dominance_rules.trigger: an engagement state is about to influence the backlog view or ordering
dominance_rules.action: hold the backlog ordered by learning need and non-punitive regardless of engagement state

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate the binding brief from the owner-open points before building any visual
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning a fixed element or inventing an answer to an open point and having to unwind it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Store the frozen day percentage regardless of the past-day visual treatment from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a data migration when the frozen-vs-gray-out UNKNOWN is later resolved

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the effort and mastery metrics on separate denominators from the first data model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: untangling a merged progress number after effort has been misread as mastery

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach freeze/repair and the secondary metric when the streak is first built, not after a break incident
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a streak-anxiety disengagement that has to be patched in production

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide informational-feedback-only (no points/prizes) before adding any reward layer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building and then stripping a tangible-reward economy that undermined intrinsic motivation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map every fill segment to real completed work at design time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fabricated-progress feature that has to be removed once flagged as manipulation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Grade every engagement claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN as it is first stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a vendor claim or an unfixed scale hardening into an assumed fact that must later be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Front-load the guardrails through the ~2-month habit window per the 66-day evidence
anti_rework_rules.prevents: dropping early protection on a false fast-habit assumption and losing the learner in the fragile phase

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner resolves an open point (5%-rounding direction, past-incomplete-day behaviour, or task weighting)
iteration_protocol.action: replace the corresponding ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN with the decided value and re-render the affected day-box states

iteration_protocol.trigger: an in-app streak-break disengagement signal is observed for this learner
iteration_protocol.action: re-tune the freeze/repair policy and the secondary-metric prominence and re-check the non-punitive contract

iteration_protocol.trigger: an independent (non-vendor) engagement or streak-retention finding replaces the Duolingo 2.4x claim
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the evidence grade on the streak rationale and re-confirm the go/no-go verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the confidence-rating scale is decided at build time or a calibration signal shows self-ratings are unreliable
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN rating-scale flag and re-derive how mastery updates the course view

iteration_protocol.trigger: the scheduler exposes a future-scheduled-load forecast worth plotting
iteration_protocol.action: add the forecast as a distinct secondary indicator and re-check it does not overload the completion box

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new engagement mechanic (e.g. a social or celebratory feature) is proposed
iteration_protocol.action: run it through the four-gate go/no-go and the non-punitive contract before any build

iteration_protocol.trigger: an in-app time-to-habit signal contradicts the ~66-day assumption for this learner
iteration_protocol.action: revise the early-protection window and the consistent-slot default
